Definition: akin to the base of G3509; gloom (as shrouding like a cloud):--blackness, darkness, mist.
BiblicalUsage: Zophos is gloom, the black darkness that shrouds like a cloud — Hebrews says believers have not come to the mount that burned with fire, nor to blackness and darkness and tempest. Peter and Jude use the same word for the fate of the fallen angels and the false teachers: the mist of darkness reserved for ever, the blackness of darkness where wandering stars burn out. It is darkness with no dawn in it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe zophos is what lies at the end of turning from the light — not mere absence, but a darkness God Himself reserves for those who refuse Him. I am glad I have come instead to Mount Zion, to Jesus, and to the blood that speaks better things.
